done_when: forge next says an item whose pull request merged is merged and names the cleanup, instead of waiting for checks, and a test proves it

findings.body: When the last task merges on GitHub before origin/<default> is fetched, this branch recommends `forge story done` using the new GitHub-derived status. However, that command reads the last-fetched ref (`src/forge/story.py:174`, `376–381`) and refuses completion when task merges are absent there (`182–186`). Removing the worktrees does not refresh that ref, so the printed sequence ends in a contradictory “not merged yet” refusal. Include a fetch before recommending story completion when merge evidence comes only from GitHub.
findings.title: Fetch merged task state before recommending story completion

why: forge next lists already-merged fixes and tasks as waiting for their checks while their worktrees still exist
